proposed_abstraction.rationale: Both functions live in a file named validators.py, share identical line span (4-10) and LOC (7), and were flagged as an exact structural match, indicating the same email-format-checking logic was copy-pasted into repo_a_payments and repo_b_orders; consolidating into one shared validator removes duplicate maintenance of email validation rules across repos.
proposed_abstraction.security_notes: The qualified_names differ in a way that suggests differing call-site conventions: 'validate_email' (repo_a_payments) may be intended to raise/assert on invalid input while 'is_valid_email' (repo_b_orders) implies a boolean-returning check — despite identical structural hashes, confirm both actually share the same return/error-handling contract before merging, and expose a single boolean-returning primitive plus a thin raising wrapper if callers rely on exception behavior. No evidence from file path, LOC, or line range of a differing regex/threshold/format constant between the two copies, but since email-format rules (e.g., allowed TLDs, max length) are often tweaked ad hoc, keep the validation pattern/constant internal to the shared implementation rather than caller-supplied unless a concrete need to parameterize it is identified.
